**= 154 (correct)**

questions.question: Which was not the part of Original Indian Constitution that was adopted in the year 1950?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• On the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, the fundamental duties were added.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 in our Indian Constitution.
 
• The 86th Amendment raised the number of fundamental obligations from 10 to 11 in 2002.
 
• Fundamental duties are addressed to the citizens whereas directive principles address the state.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Emergency Provisions

 
 
• Emergency Provisions are contained in Part Eighteen of the Constitution of India.

 
 
• The President of India has the power to impose emergency rules in any or all the Indian states if the security of part or all of India is threatened by "war or external aggression or armed rebellion".
 
 
 
• The Constitution stipulates three types of emergencies:
 
 
• National Emergency
 
• Constitutional Emergency
 
• Financial Emergency
 
 
 
 

 
• Directive Principles of State Policy

 
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are stated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It contains Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSPs are non-binding in nature which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• These principles emphasize that the State shall try to promote the welfare of the people by providing them basic facilities like shelter, food and clothing.
 
• It denotes the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.
 
• Article 51 is the last Directive Principle of State Policy in the Constitution.
 
 

 
• Fundamental Rights

 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35). Part III of the Constitution is described as the Magna Carta of India.
 
• ‘Magna Carta’, the Charter of Rights issued by King John of England in 1215 was the first written document relating to the Fundamental Rights of citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are justiciable because when violated the aggrieved individual can move the courts for their enforcement.
 
• The Supreme Court or High Courts have the power to issue directions or orders or writs for the enforcement of any of the Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of earthquake wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P-waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Earthquake: 

__
 
• An earthquake (also known as a quake, tremor, or temblor) is the shaking of the surface of the Earth resulting from a sudden release of energy in the Earth's lithosphere that creates seismic waves
 
• There are two types of earthquake, 
 
 
• Body wave: 'P' wave and 'S' wave
 
• Surface wave: 'L' wave and 'R' wave
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6c65456702f76c756160752cb845963bdccf7379fbb8c83f885fb21fe48f83b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Earthquake wave
 Characteristics
 
 

 P - waves
 
 
 
• P-wave is one of the two main types of elastic body waves, called seismic waves in seismology.
 
• Also known as the primary wave or the pressure wave.
 
• P-waves travel faster than other seismic waves and hence are the first signal from an earthquake to arrive at any affected location or at a seismograph.
 
• P-waves may be transmitted through gases, liquids, or solids.
 
 
 
 

 S - waves
 
 
 
• S-waves are transverse waves that move perpendicular to the direction of propagation.
 
• S-waves are slower than P-waves.
 
• Therefore, they appear later than P-waves on a seismogram.
 
• Fluids cannot support the perpendicular motion, so S-waves only travel in solids.
 
 
 
 

 R - waves
 
 
 
• Also known as the Rayleigh wave.
 
• It has both compressional and shear motions.
 
• These waves result from the interaction of P-waves and vertically polarized S-waves with the surface and can exist in any solid medium.
 
 
 
 

 L - waves
 
 
 
• Also known as love wave
 
• It is a purely shear wave.
 
• These waves are formed by horizontally polarized S-waves interacting with the surface, and can only exist if there is a change in the elastic properties with depth in a solid medium, which is always the case in seismological applications. 
 
• This is more destructive at the epicenter.

__
 
• **Clayey soil **has a** high proportion of fine particles and typically feels smooth and sticky to the touch when wet.**
 
• Due to the fine particles,** clayey soil has small pore spaces, which reduces the rate of water drainage and can lead to waterlogging.**
 
• This type of **soil is often rich in nutrients because it can retain water and dissolved nutrients very well, although its poor drainage can sometimes be detrimental to certain plants.**
 
• **Clayey soil** is generally heavy and compact, **making it harder to work with, especially when wet.**
 
• Howeve**r, when managed well, clayey soils can be very fertile and are suitable for crops like rice that require a lot of water.**

 Soil Type
 Characteristics
 
 
 
 

 Sandy Soil
 
 
Sandy soil has a high proportion of sand particles and feels gritty to the touch.

 
It has good drainage and aeration but doesn't retain water and nutrients well, which makes it less fertile than other soil types.

 
 
 

 Watery Soil
 
 
This isn't a standard classification of soil. However, waterlogged soils can be an issue in certain situations.

 
These soils are saturated with water for long periods, which can deprive plant roots of oxygen and lead to the death of plants.

 
 
 

 Loamy Soil
 
 
Loamy soil is a well-balanced mixture of sand, silt, and clay particles.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 9 km/h, while the stream’s speed is 1.5 km/h. A man rows to a location 105 km away and then returns to his starting position. The total time taken by him is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Speed of boat in still water = 9 km/h

Speed of stream = 1.5 km/h

Distance = 105 km

**Concept:**

Time is calculated as distance/speed.

**Calculation: **

Time is taken to go upstream = Distance/Speed upstream

105 km/(9 km/h - 1.5 km/h) = 14 hours

Time is taken to come downstream = Distance/Speed downstream

105 km/(9 km/h + 1.5 km/h) = 10 hours

Total time is 14 + 10 = 24 hours.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

Find the number of days in which Q alone can do the total work.
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

P can complete the work in = 200 days

Q and R together can complete the work in = 100 days

P, Q, and R work together for = 40 days

P and R finish the remaining work in = 40 days

**Concept:**

This problem is related to work and time. The total work done is the product of the rate of work and the time.

**Calculation:**

Work done by P in 1 day = 1/200

⇒ Work done by Q and R in 1 day = 1/100

⇒ Work done by P, Q, and R in 40 days = 40 × (1/200 + 1/100) = 2/3 of the total work

⇒ Therefore, work done by P and R in 40 days = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the total work

⇒ Work done by P and R in 1 day = (1/3)/40 = 1/120

⇒ So, work done by Q in 1 day = 1/100 - 1/200 = 1/200

⇒ Time taken by Q alone to do the work = 1/(1/200) = 200 days

**Therefore, Q alone can do the total work in 200 days.**

questions.question: The average of 7 natural numbers is 70. Among them six numbers are 32, 69, 72, 65, 79, 48. What is the seventh number?

Average of seven numbers = 70

Six numbers = 32, 69, 72, 65, 79, 48

The total of seven numbers can be calculated by multiplying the average with 7. Subtracting the sum of given six numbers from this total gives the seventh number.

Total of seven numbers = Average × 7 = 70 × 7 = 490.

questions.question: A car driver is driving car at a speed of 70 km/h and a bus is moving 35 metres ahead of him. After 15 seconds, the bus is 40 metres behind of him. Find the speed of the bus.
questions.solution:

Speed of car = 70 km/h

Distance ahead initially = 35 m

Distance behind after 15 seconds = 40 m

**Concept:**

Relative speed and basic physics (Speed = Distance/Time)

**Calculation:**

Speed of car in m/s = 70 × 1000/3600 = 19.44 m/s

In 15 seconds, distance covered by car = 19.44 × 15 = 291.6 m

Distance covered by bus in 15 seconds = 291.6 - 35 (initial lead) - 40 (final lag) = 216.6 m

Speed of bus = Distance/Time = 216.6/15 = 14.44 m/s

Speed of bus in km/h = 14.44 × 3600/1000 = 51.984 km/h ≈ 52 km/h

**Therefore, the speed of the bus is approximately 52 km/h.**

questions.question: In an election contested by two parties, party A secured 16 percent of the total votes more than party B. If party B got 25200 votes and there are no invalid votes, by how many votes did party B lose the election?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total number of votes be 100%.

The margin of loss is given as 16%, so Party B's vote share = (100% − 16%) ÷ 2 = 42%.

We are given that 42% of total votes = 25200.

Party B lost by the difference of 16%.

Margin of loss = (25200 ÷ 42) × 16 = 600 × 16 = 9600 votes.

**∴ The correct answer is 9600 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Difference in vote percentage between Party A and Party B = 16% of total votes

Votes secured by Party B = 25200

There are no invalid votes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3276f37536c2a7ec8ba9869f5baec29677757c79efa718fd58d5dc409f6db115.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of votes be 100%.

⇒ Votes of Party A − Votes of Party B = 16%

⇒ Votes of Party A + Votes of Party B = 100%

⇒ Substitute Party A's share: (Votes of Party B + 16%) + Votes of Party B = 100%

⇒ 2 × Votes of Party B = 100% − 16% = 84%

⇒ Votes of Party B = 42%

⇒ According to the question, 42% of Total Votes = 25200

⇒ 1% of Total Votes = 25200 ÷ 42 = 600

⇒ Party B lost by the difference in votes, which is exactly 16% of total votes.

⇒ Margin of loss = 16 × 600 = 9600 votes.

**∴ The correct answer is 9600 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Base Concept

In election problems, the total valid votes are always considered as 100%. If there are only two candidates and no invalid votes, the winner's percentage and loser's percentage will always sum up to exactly 100%.

Winning Margin

The margin by which a candidate wins or loses the election is given by the direct difference between their respective vote percentages. Winning Margin = Winner% − Loser%.

Invalid Votes Rule

When invalid votes are present, Total Cast Votes = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes. Candidates' shares are usually calculated as a percentage of valid votes, unless the question explicitly specifies it as a percentage of total registered voters.
